page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, this instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes 77 GB of local SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2701.48. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 2701.48 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 2149.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, reflecting the physical limitation of its single-core, dual-thread hardware configuration. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth registering at 140.21 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 22.5 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while complex workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations score in the lower performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ads_v5 offers a high memory-to-core density, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. The inclusion of 77 GB of local storage provides a resource-dense configuration for temporary data. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is best suited for light database operations, memory-intensive caching, basic web serving, and single-threaded background tasks where RAM capacity is prioritized over multi-core compute performance.
